# Bump the release version

One PR that moves every place carrying bit's release version and nothing else, and the issue it closes.

## First, check the checkout is up to date

Fetch `origin` and work on a new branch cut from `origin/develop`, in its own worktree so the maintainer's checkout stays
as it is. Read this file and the helper from that checkout.

## Pick the version and the issue

The current version is `ReleaseVersion` in `src/Bit.Build.props`. Prerelease issues carry the `prerelease` label,
releases the `release` label; look at the latest few. If the next version already has an open PR, report that PR and
stop. If it has an issue and no PR, use the issue. Otherwise open one titled ``Prerelease `v-X.Y.Z-pre-NN` `` or ``Release `v-X.Y.Z` ``, with the same text as its body,
that label, and yourself as assignee. Prerelease numbers have two digits. When it is unclear what comes next (another
pre, the stable release, or the first pre of a new version), ask.

## Where the version lives

Two kinds of place:

- **Full**: the release version itself, moved on every bump. Bit.* package references and package versions,
  `ReleaseVersion`, the `Bit.Cli` install and `dnx` commands in docs, pages, scripts and the dev container, the version
  literals of the scripts and service workers, version constants, the `@v-` refs to bit's own GitHub actions, the
  templates' "Generated by" headers, the Boilerplate's `bit.json`, the default of the bit-setup action, and the
  dependency-update skill's note on our own version.
- **Core**: only major.minor.patch, moved only when that changes (from a stable release to the next version's first pre,
  or to a patch). These are the `bitplatform.dev/mcp?v=` URLs in the coding agents' MCP configs.

A plain search and replace only works while the version is a unique prerelease string. A stable `X.Y.Z` is shared with
Microsoft packages of the same major after its GA, version ranges, changelog headings, examples and test data, and the
core places hold a bare `X.Y.Z` all through the prereleases. The set of files also changes between bumps as projects
are added, moved or removed.

`.github/agents/version-bump/version-bump.ps1` (PowerShell 7) works from what sits next to it:

- `rules.json`: each place as a line rule, a regex holding `{V}` (full) or `{CORE}` (core) exactly once, the file
  patterns it applies to (`*` also crosses folders), and why it exists.
- `reviewed.json`: lines that look like ours but are not, as the file and the whole trimmed line, with why.
- `locations.json`: every file and line pattern the rules match today, version free, so each bump PR's diff on it shows
  which places came or went.

## Scan

Run the helper with `scan` and make it clean before bumping:

- **UNCOVERED** (only while the current version is a prerelease, where a plain search is the truth): an occurrence no
  rule matches, so a new kind of place. Add a rule with enough context that it could never match someone else's line
  at a stable version. Never widen a rule into "any line with the version".
- **SUSPECTS**: a bare version next to a bit hint that no rule matches. Ours: a rule. Not ours: a `reviewed.json` entry.
- **Compared with locations.json**: files and lines that came or went since the last bump. New demos and moved
  projects are expected; make sure each one makes sense.
- A rule that matches nothing: delete it once its place is gone for good.

Doing this on every prerelease is the point: by the stable release, where a plain search no longer tells ours from
theirs, the rules are already complete.

## Bump

Run `bump -To <version>`, with `-DryRun` first when in doubt. It refuses while anything is uncovered, and while
suspects are open when the bump moves a bare version (a stable version on either side, or the core moving). It keeps
every file's encoding, BOM and line endings, checks that `ReleaseVersion` moved, that no old prerelease string is left,
and that the rules match as many places after the bump as before, then rewrites `locations.json`.

Read the diff: every changed line is a version line, apart from the helper's own files.

The build has a net of its own: projects list the files with a hand-written copy of the version as
`ReleaseVersionLiteral`, and the build fails when one of them does not hold `ReleaseVersion`.

## Things a bump does not do

- A comment that needs an example version uses a made-up one, never the current version, or the next bump rewrites it.
- The first pre of a new version may need a new heading in BlazorUI's `BreakingChanges.md`. The people who make the
  breaking changes write it, not the bump; mention it if it is missing.
- Merging, tagging (a `v-*-pre-*` tag publishes the prerelease packages) and the stable publish from `main` stay with
  the maintainers.

## Commit and PR

Branch `<your-login>/<issue>/prerelease-v-X.Y.Z-pre-NN` (or `release-v-X.Y.Z`). Commit
`feat(prerelease): v-X.Y.Z-pre-NN #<issue>` or `feat(release): v-X.Y.Z #<issue>`. PR title
`Prerelease v-X.Y.Z-pre-NN (#<issue>)` or `Release v-X.Y.Z (#<issue>)`, body `closes #<issue>`, base `develop`. The
title must start with Prerelease or Release: that is what starts All Release Build on the PR.

## Done when

The scan was clean before the bump, the PR is open with only version lines (plus any rule or list updates), and the
report names the issue and the PR, how many files and lines moved, and which places came or went since the last bump.
